attributes.title: 2027 Annual Conference of the American Psychology-Law Society
attributes.summary:
The American Psychology-Law Society, Division 41 of the American Psychological Association, meets in Louisville, Kentucky, from March 18 to 20, 2027, at the Louisville Marriott Downtown. Optional preconference workshops run the day before, on Wednesday, March 17. The main program follows the society's usual pattern: a welcome reception Thursday evening, a Friday morning plenary with paper, symposium and poster sessions, and Saturday sessions with a data blitz and closing events.

The meeting draws forensic and clinical psychologists, researchers, attorneys and graduate students working on topics such as competency and risk assessment, eyewitness memory, jury decision-making and correctional mental health. The call for proposals closed on October 15, 2026, and the detailed schedule is due in early 2027.

Online registration opens in early 2027. The society lists rates based on 2026, which may change: full members pay $345 before January 31 and $380 after, non-members $490 and $575, and student members $90 and $125, with separate rates for early-career members, non-member students and the workshops. The conference page does not state continuing education credit, so psychologists who need CE should confirm with the society before registering.
